module_title: OSI Model & Network Devices - Foundational Basics
introduction: To understand how data travels from one computer to another across the globe, a universal standard was created called the 'OSI Model'. At this foundational level, we will define this model and explore the two most basic devices used to connect computers together: Hubs and Switches.

core_concepts.title: The OSI Model
core_concepts.description: OSI stands for 'Open Systems Interconnection'. Introduced by the ISO (International Organization for Standardization) in 1984, it is a conceptual framework used to describe the functions of a networking system. It is vertically divided into 7 distinct layers.

core_concepts.title: Hub (The 'Dumb' Device)
core_concepts.description: A basic networking device used to connect multiple computers in a single Local Area Network (LAN). It is considered 'dumb' because it cannot filter data. If Computer A sends a message to Computer B, the Hub blindly copies and 'Broadcasts' that message to EVERY computer connected to it.

core_concepts.title: Switch (The 'Smart' Device)
core_concepts.description: A Switch also connects computers within a single LAN, but it is 'smart'. It learns and memorizes the physical address (MAC Address) of every connected computer. When Computer A sends a message to Computer B, the Switch delivers it ONLY to Computer B ('Unicast'), reducing network traffic.

important_entities.name: 7 Layers
important_entities.significance: Data passes through these layers sequentially. A highly repeated Tier-1 question is simply asking for the total number of layers in the OSI model. The answer is always exactly 7.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: Do not confuse the two! The OSI model is a theoretical reference model with strictly 7 layers. The TCP/IP model is the practical, real-world model that runs the Internet, and it only has 4 (or sometimes categorized as 5) layers.

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: A Hub 'hollers' (broadcasts) the message to everyone in the room. A Switch 'whispers' (unicasts) the message directly into the ear of the specific receiver.

exam_strategy_tips: In preliminary exams, if asked 'Which networking device broadcasts data to all connected ports?', select Hub. Always memorize the full expansion of OSI: Open Systems Interconnection.
